Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle along with the Netherlands players. Paul Stirling and Kevin O'Brien are the openers for Ireland. Fred Klaassen to start proceedings with the ball.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then! 106 runs needed in 120 balls and it will be very interesting to see how the veteran openers of Ireland will proceed with the innings. Will they go bang from the very first ball? We shall find out soon as the second half is just on the other side.

The hero with the ball, Curtis Campher, is down for a chat, he says that it was just good to be out in the park and play cricket. Mentions that he wasn't feeling great after the first over but that one over where he got 4 wickets changed everything. Tells that Andy Balbirnie gives him the freedom to do whatever he wants to.

This has been a sparkling bowling performance from Ireland. Not just from Curtis Campher but as a whole group. They were accurate throughout the innings with their lines and lengths and continued to chip wickets in regular intervals. Who else but Curtis Campher ran the show today with the ball as he scalped 4 wickets in 4 balls. Nothing to take away from the brilliance of Mark Adair, as he too chipped in 3 wickets while giving away just 9 runs - the most economical figures by an Irishman in T20 World Cup history.

Not the best performance from Netherlands, after opting to bat first. Max O'Dowd was the wall for the Netherlands, because of his composed innings. Netherlands have managed to reach a total which still looks like below par. They had a nervy start as they lost Ben Cooper early on. Bas de Leede also followed him and then Colin Ackermann tried to steady the ship but he too fail to make any impact. It was then the brilliance of Curtis Campher which killed the middle order in a blink of an eye. Max O'Dowd did his best but he too fell after making his half-century. In the end, it was their skipper, Pieter Seelaar who helped his team crawl to an inferior total.

This is an excellent performance from Ireland as they have shown what they are capable of. Their bowlers have been top-notch from the word go and they will be very happy going into the break. Curtis Campher has joined an elite list of players to pick 4 wickets in 4 balls. Lasith Malinga, Rashid Khan and now Curtis Campher. He also becomes the first bowler to achieve this feat in T20 World Cups. Absolute gun bowling display from the 22-year-old.

OUT! TAKEN! Earlier, Curtis Campher got a hat-trick and now Ireland gets a team hat-trick. Mark Adair bowls a short-of-a-length ball, outside off. Brandon Glover goes down on his knee to heave it away but gets a top edge. The ball goes high up in the air towards mid off. Curtis Campher settles himself under it and gulps it down. NETHERLANDS FINISH WITH 106!
Commentary.Howout: c Curtis Campher b Mark Adair

Commentary.Commentary: Brandon Glover is the last man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Another one bites the dust for Netherlands. Full and straight, Logan van Beek clips it towards deep mid-wicket. The batters set off for the second very quickly but Josh Little is onto the ball in a flash at the fence. Little throws it on the bounce to Neil Rock, the keeper. Rock whips off the bails and van Beek is well short and has to depart.
Run out appeal taken upstairs. Logan van Beek puts a big dive at the keeper's end but he still fails short of his crease and now he has to depart.
Fred Klaassen is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mark Adair has been brilliant out there with the ball. Pitched up, on off stump and Pieter Seelaar just had to go for the big shot. Seelaar mistimes it badly and chips it towards long on. Andy Balbirnie runs in from the deep and takes a good low catch. Mark Adair gets his second wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Andy Balbirnie b Mark Adair

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, whipped across to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Lovely change of pace again from Adair. On a length, around off and completely bamboozles Logan van Beek as he misses his swipe across.
Pitched up, on middle. Van Beek pushes it towards wide long on and races back for the second. Excellent running.
Mark Adair to bowl the final over.
Short of a length, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.

LEG BYE! Little misses the shy at the stumps yet again. Pieter Seelaar walks right across hi stumps and Little follows him with a fuller delivery. Seelaar misses the scoop and gets hit on the pads. Van Beek calls him for the single and they take off. Little misses at the non-striker's end and Seelaar survives.

Logan van Beek was a goner if that hit! Fullish ball, around off. Seelaar bunts it back to the bowler and van Beek was well outside his crease. Josh Little picks it up and misses from close range. He should have hit from there!
A wide yorker this time, well executed. Pieter Seelaar can't reach it and again, no wide called.
Full and wide again, van Beek can't get under it and manages to heave it down to long off for a single.
Very full and very wide, van Beek was already outside the off stump and missed the drive. No wide called.
Josh Little is back into the attack.
On middle and pushed down the ground for one. 9 runs from the over.
Flatter one, around off. Van Beek dabs it towards third man and races back for the single.
Tossed up, around off. Pieter Seelaar goes over cover and picks up a single.

FOUR! Simi Singh tries to bowl a leg spinner delivery but drags it down on leg stump. Pieter Seelaar rocks back and picks his spot as he pulls it to the right of the fielder at deep square leg. A welcome boundary for Netherlands.
Flighted ball, on off and Logan van Beek eases it down to long on for a run.
On off and pushed back to the bowler.
Simi Singh is back for his final over.
Another single to end the over. Back of a length, on middle. Logan van Beek dabs it down to fine leg. Just 3 runs and a wicket off it.
Another slower delivery, around off. Pieter Seelaar waits for it and then nudges it behind point for a single.
A length ball, around off. Pieter Seelaar gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.
Who walks out? It is Logan van Beek.

OUT! CAUGHT! That is the last thing Netherlands would have wished for right now. Slower one and this is pushed fuller and well wider. Max O'Dowd goes after it and looks to clear long on. Max O'Dowd does get the elevation but not the distance and Harry Tector takes a well judged catch at the long on fence. Mark Adair gets his first wicket of the day.
Commentary.Howout: c Harry Tector b Mark Adair

Commentary.Commentary: Full and wide, Max O'Dowd bunts it back to the bowler.
Length ball, on top of off and hit down the ground for a single.
Mark Adair is back on.
Full and on off, drilled to long off for one.
Half tracker on middle, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Flatter and on middle, Pieter Seelaar chops it towards point for a single.
Floats it up, outside off. Pieter Seelaar chips it past cover for a brace.
FIFTY! Benjamin White tosses it up, on middle. Max O'Dowd clips it to long on for a single. He reamins the key for Netherlands if they aim for a respectable total.
On the pads, tucked to deep square leg for a single.
Benjamin White (2-0-20-0) is back into the attack.

Length ball, on off. Pieter Seelaar mistimes his heave to mid on and takes off for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. End of an excellent spell from Curtis Campher. 4-0-26-4 from him.
Good-length ball, on off. Pieter Seelaar pushes it to extra cover.
Good-length ball, on middle and leg. Max O'Dowd looks to tuck it on the leg side. He gets an inside edge onto the pads. The batters scamper across for a quick single.
On a good length, on off. Max O'Dowd taps it towards point.
Length ball, on off. Max O'Dowd defends it on the off side.
FOUR! Poor delivery from Curtis Campher. Bowls it full and on the pads, Max O'Dowd tickles it to fine leg for a boundary.
Change! Curtis Campher to end his spell here.
Loopy ball, on off. Pieter Seelaar pats it to the right of the bowler. Simi Singh dives that side and stops the ball.
Drags the length back and bowls it short, on off. Max O'Dowd punches it to long on off the back foot for a single.
Simi Singh sees Pieter Seelaar charging down the track and bowls it down the leg side. Pieter Seelaar does it well to nudge it on the leg side for a single.
Tosses it up, on off. Pieter Seelaar knocks it back to the bowler.
Flatter ball, outside off. Max O'Dowd eases it down to long on for one.
On middle, Max O'Dowd turns it to mid-wicket.
Simi Singh is back into the attack.
Floats it up, on middle. Tucked on the leg side. Max O'Dowd retains the strike by picking up a single.

FOUR! Two in a row! Short and on middle, Max O'Dowd rocks back and thumps this one away to deep mid-wicket. The fielder there runs to his left and dives but couldn't prevent the ball from reaching the boundary.
FOUR! Nicely played! Loopy ball, on middle. Max O'Dowd smashes it straight down the ground towards long on for a boundary.
Full and on off, driven towards extra cover.
WIDE! Short and way too outside off, Max O'Dowd leaves it alone. Wided.
Slower through the air, outside off. Max O'Dowd steers it to deep cover for a couple of runs.
Floats it up, outside off. Max O'Dowd taps it to point.
Benjamin White (1-0-8-0) is back into the attack.
Full and on the pads, flicked to deep square leg for one more.
This was way outside off, on a length. Max O'Dowd reaches and tries to cut it but fails to get any bat on it.
On a length, on middle. Pieter Seelaar nudges it on the leg side for one run.
FOUR! EDGY RUNS! A length ball, outside off. Pieter Seelaar loos to cut but gets a thick outside edge and the ball runs down to the third man fence.
On a length and angling on the pads. Pieter Seelaar looks to pull but gets hit high on the pads.
PLAY AND A MISS! A length ball, outside off. Pieter Seelaar looks to drive but gets fails to connect it.
Slight fuller, outside off. Pieter Seelaar works it down to third man for a single.
On a length, on off. Pieter Seelaar blocks it back on the deck.
A length ball, outside off. Pieter Seelaar dabs it to backward point.
A length ball, outside off. Pieter Seelaar skips down and shoulders arms to it.
Short of a length outside off. Pieter Seelaar misses his pull.
On a length, on off. Pieter Seelaar hits it to covers.
Josh Little (2-0-11-1) is back into the attack.
Full ball, on off, pushed through covers for a single. Pieter Seelaar is off the mark.
The skipper, Pieter Seelaar is in early, at number 8.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Curtis Campher, take a bow! Four in four for him. This time he delivers a length ball, outside off. Roelof van der Merwe reaches out for it and looks to drive but gets an inside edge. The ball crashes onto the stumps and wickets falling like a pack of cards for Netherlands. Curtis Campher becomes the third bowler in T20 history to bag four in four after Lasith Malinga and Rashid Khan. Absolute scenes out there in Abu Dhabi.
Roelof van der Merwe wlaks out to bat with Netherlands in all sorts of trouble.

Ireland have taken the review for an LBW decision. UltraEdge confirms that there's no bat involved. Ball Tracking shows that the ball is indeed hitting the leg stump. OUT is the decision. Unreal review and Curtis Campher has a hat-trick!

OUT! A deja vu delivery from Curtis Campher to Scott Edwards and he is given LBW. HAT-TRICK FOR CURTIS CAMPHER. Campher serves another full ball, this one angling on middle and leg. Scott Edwards looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. Curtis Campher appeals his heart out but the umpire is not interested. Campher convinces his captain to take the review and it shows three reds on Ball Tracker. Scott Edwards has been given LBW and Campher has a Hat-Trick. A terrific over from Curtis Campher.
Scott Edwards comes out to face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! LBW! A beauty of a delivery from Curtis Campher as the main man of Netherlands goes back for a golden duck. Campher steams and serves a full ball, very full angling on middle. Ryan ten Doeschate is too late to respond as he looks to flick but misses it out completely. He gets hit on the pads. An appeal and an easy decision for the umpire as it looked plumbed to the naked eye. No need for the review and Ryan ten Doeschate walks back. Curtis Campher is on a Hat-Trick.
Ryan ten Doeschate is the new man in.
Ireland have taken the DRS for a caught behind decision. UltraEdge shows that there's a spike as the ball passes the gloves and the third umpire asks the onfield umpire to reverse his decision. OUT!

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! This has been a brilliant bowling display from Ireland till now. Campher hurls in and bowls a back-of-a-length delivery, angling down on the leg side. Colin Ackermann hangs back and looks to pull but seems to miss it. They appeal for caught behind but the umpire signals it wide instead. Ireland take the review. UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball passes the gloves and this is a brilliant review from Ireland. Netherlands in a spot of bother as they lose their third wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Neil Rock b Curtis Campher

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on off, slapped to covers.
WIDE! Campher starts with a full ball down the leg side. Colin Ackermann misses his whip.
Curtis Campher (1-0-12-0) is back into the attack.
Now goes on the back foot and hits this flatter ball towards covers.
50 up for Netherlands! A full ball, on ff. Colin Ackermann skips down and nudges it to long on for a single.
Loopy ball, outside off. Max O'Dowd works it to covers for a single.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Tossed up ball, full and around off. Max O'Dowd waits and then smashes it straight down to long on for a boundary.
Goes full now and on middle. Colin Ackermann sweeps it to deep square leg for a single.
A flatter ball, outside off. Max O'Dowd pushes it through covers for a single.
A touch shorter, around off. Max O'Dowd works it through mid-wicket for one.
Ackermann gives himself room and Singh follows him. Ackermann manages to work it down the ground for a single.
Flatter one, clipped through square leg for one.
On the pads, Max O'Dowd taps it back to the bowler.
Simi Singh sees Colin Ackermann advancing and shortens the length and bowls it on the pads. Ackermann gets an inside edge towards short fine leg. They get a single.
Tossed up, on leg stump. Max O'Dowd pushes it down the ground for a single.
Simi Singh is back into the attack.
Lucky for Curtis Campher as this could have been another boundary. A half-volley on off stump. Colin Ackermann brings out the cover drive but the fielder at extra cover does well to stop it.
FOUR! Another freebie from Curtis Campher. Length again, well outside off. Colin Ackermann cuts hard and beats third man to his right. Second boundary of the over.
WIDE! On leg stump and angling further down the leg side. Ackermann misses the flick and a wide is signalled.
Full and on off, Max O'Dowd presents the full face of the bat and eases it down to long off for another single.
Back of a length, outside off. Colin Ackermann dabs it down through cover-point and collects a single.
Wide again but its a bit fuller this time, Max O'Dowd strokes it away to deep point for one.
FOUR! Width on offer and Max O'Dowd doesn't miss out on it. Short and wide, cut away to the vacant point boundary.
Curtis Campher is into the attack.
A fifth dot on the trot to end the over! Length ball, on middle and Colin Ackermann mistimes his pull to mid-wicket. Netherlands are 25/2 at the end of the Powerplay.
That one moved away quite a bit after pitching. Banged in short, around off and the ball moves away sharply. Ackermann leaves it alone.
Excellent line and length. On top of off and Ackermann can only manage to keep it out on the off side.
A well directed bumper this time from Mark Adair. Colin Ackermann sways his head away from the ball.
Good-length ball, outside off. Ackermann taps it to backward point.
Pitched up, on middle and wristed away on the leg side for a single.
Mark Adair is back on.
Back of a length, outside off. Colin Ackermann hangs back and steers it through the backward point region for a couple of runs.
Nice shot for no run. Around off and Colin Ackermann plays a classy cover drive straight to the fielder.
Colin Ackermann is the new man in.

OUT! Cleaned up! Bas de Leede will be kicking himself after that shot. Josh Little hurls across a full toss, angling in on leg stump. Bas de Leede walks right across his stumps and looks to ramp it over short fine leg. The ball is too quick for him and he misses it completely. The ball crashes into leg stump and sends it flying. Netherlands lose their second and Josh Little has his man.
FOUR! Here comes the release shot. Bas de Leede was bogged down and so he decides to advance down the track. On a length, on off and swatted back past the bowler for a boundary.
Little comes around the wicket and serves a length ball, on off. Bas de Leede makes a bit of room but can't get it through the inner ring on the off side.
Little hits the length hard, around off. De Leede dabs it down to point.
Josh Little is back into the attack. Went for 5 runs in his first over.
Better line from Simi Singh! Floats it up, on off. Max O'Dowd clips it to wide of long on for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Superb shot! Tossed up delivery, outside off. Max O'Dowd makes room for himself and lofts it over covers for a gorgeous boundary.
On leg, nudged to mid on for a run.
Loopy ball, on middle. Max O'Dowd strides forward and drives it towards covers for a single.
Flighted delivery, outside off. Pushed to long on for a run.
Tosses it up, on off. Max O'Dowd steps out and nudges it to mid on for one.
Change from both ends now as Simi Singh is into the attack now.
Back of a length, on off. Bas de Leede hops and blocks it out from the crease.

Length ball, down the leg side. Bas de Leede looks to tuck it on the leg side but misses. Mark Adair and Neil Rock appeal for a caught behind but the umpire shakes his head. Replay shows that the ball brushed off his thigh pad.
Short of a length, on off. Max O'Dowd charges down the track and smashes it to mid on. Only a single.
Good-length ball, on middle. Max O'Dowd looks to hit it on the leg side but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Length ball, outside off. Max O'Dowd pushes it straight towards covers.
Full and on middle, attacking the stumps. Max O'Dowd blocks it out.
Change! Mark Adair is into the attack.
Good-length ball, outside off. Bas de Leede looks to drive but misses.

Fuller in length, on the pads. Max O'Dowd looks to flick but misses. He gets hit on the pads. The ball rolls on the leg side and the batters sneak a single. Josh Little appeals for an LBW but the umpire says no.
FOUR! Top shot! Short of a length and outside off. Max O'Dowd gets on top of the bounce and thumps it through cover-point for a boundary.
Full, outside off. Max O'Dowd plays the cover drive but mistimes it.
Back of a length, outside off. Bas de Leede rocks back and dabs it towards backward point for one.
Fullish ball, around off and driven straight to covers.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is Josh Little.
Tossed up, on off and Max O'Dowd blocks it out. An eventful first over comes to an end.
And again. Lovely flighted ball, outside off, angled in but drifting away at the last moment. Max O'Dowd is beaten on the outside edge.
Quicker one, outside off. This one drifts away a bit and Max O'Dowd misses the cut.
Bas de Leede walks out at number 3.
A run out appeal has been taken upstairs as Paul Stirling clips the bails off. The big screen shows the replay and it shows Ben Cooper is well short of his crease!

OUT! RUN OUT What just happened there? Stirling bowls a loopy ball, on the pads. Ben Cooper tucks it to short fine leg. Max O'Dowd takes off for a single but Ben Cooper is too late to respond. Simi Singh collects the ball and throws it at the bowler's end. Paul Stirling collects the ball and whips the bails off. But Paul Stirling dislodged one of the bails on his own before collecting the ball. The third umpire is called and luckily for Ireland, the second bail was whipped off with the ball in his palms. Ben Cooper will have to walk back to the pavilion. An early blow for Netherlands!
Netherlands and Max O'Dowd are underway! Stirling floats it up, on middle. Max O'Dowd works it to mid on for a single.
Paul Stirling starts with a loopy ball, outside off. Max O'Dowd pushes it towards covers.

We are all set for the action. Both the teams stride out to the middle for their respective national anthems. It will be Netherlands national anthem first, followed by Ireland's. Done with the proceedings, it is time for the action to start as Max O'Dowd and Ben Cooper are the openers for Netherlands. Paul Stirling to start with the ball. Here we go...

Andy Balbirnie, the skipper of Ireland, says that he's not too disappointed with bowling first and the pitch will probably stay the same over 40 overs. Adds that the first game of the tournament is important, they are excited for it. Mentions the middle order is inexperienced but they are expressive and will look to play their shots.

Pieter Seelaar, the skipper of Netherlands, says they are going to bat first. Says that the wicket is good to bat on and they want to get some runs on the board and put Ireland under pressure. Adds that they are in Dubai for a while and have trained here. Tells that many players are coming into the team after playing county cricket.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Neil Rock (WK), Paul Stirling, Andy Balbirnie (C), Kevin O'Brien, Gareth Delany, Harry Tector, Simi Singh, Curtis Campher, Mark Adair, Josh Little, Benjamin White.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Scott Edwards (WK), Ben Cooper, Max O'Dowd, Bas de Leede, Roelof van der Merwe, Ryan ten Doeschate, Pieter Seelaar (C), Colin Ackermann, Logan van Beek, Fred Klaassen, Brandon Glover.
TOSS - Netherlands have won the toss and have elected to BAT first.

Ireland failed to qualify for Super 10 in the 2016 T20 World Cup but this time under the leadership of Andy Balbirnie, the squad looks much stronger and better. The Irish team has evolved as a team in the last few years and have some experienced pros such as Paul Stirling, George Dockrell, Andy Balbirnie, and Kevin O'Brien. They also have a few young guns in their squad who possess a better understanding of the game as far as the shortest format is concerned. Ireland have not won a T20 World Cup game against Netherlands so far and they would be keen to get a win here. Will they be able to do so? We will find out. Stay tuned for toss and further updates as this game promises to be a nutcracker.

Many fans will remember how the Dutch side famously chased a target of 190 in just 13.5 overs in the 2014 T20 World Cup qualifying round and booked themselves a place in the Super 10. The Dutch team leads the head-to-head record by 2-0 against Ireland in T20 World Cup matches as well. They also won the 2019 T20 World Cup qualifiers in the UAE which laid their path to this tournament. They have a good unit of players who can be very effective and have the ability to catch teams off-guard, especially in the T20 format.

The T20 World Cup has started with a bang with Oman and Scotland getting first hand on victory in Group B and now it's time for Group A match where Ireland and Netherlands are set to lock horns in Match 3 of the T20 World Cup qualifiers. Ireland played two warm-up matches before heading into this fixture and won both of them. While Netherlands started the warm-up matches with a hefty defeat at the hands of Scotland but bounced back with a win against Oman. Both teams would look to carry forward the winning momentum and kickstart their campaign on a winning note. On that note, welcome to the coverage.
